reason: The cited evidence supports L12 precipitation and its strengthening effect, but provides no support for the key premises that multi-stage aging can preferentially localize precipitates at boundaries, that such precipitates would act as dislocation sinks, or that dislocation pile-ups are the primary cause of brittleness. The evidence even notes precipitate-free channels near interfaces, which contradicts the proposed mechanism.
premises: L12 precipitates can be formed in Al0.7CoCrFeNi by aging
L12 precipitates increase strength in this alloy
Dislocation pile-ups at lamellar boundaries cause brittleness
Precipitates can be preferentially located at lamellar boundaries by multi-stage aging
Precipitates at boundaries will act as dislocation sinks and reduce stress concentrations
